page.part.sub: Warframe / weapon parts → where they drop
home.lead: Jump to any page from here.
guide.lead: What you can do on each page. Press Open to go to it.
guide.item: Type a material name (Japanese, English or hiragana) to list the missions, enemies, bounties and relics that drop it, with chances.
guide.part: Type the name of a Warframe, weapon or other item, or one of its blueprints or parts (Japanese, English or hiragana) to list the missions, enemies, bounties and relics that drop it, with chances. Narrow the candidates by category (same as the Mastery list). Check "Exclude Prime" to hide items that come from relics (Prime blueprints and parts). Items from clan research (with the lab), Simaris offerings and quest rewards are also listed. Items found in none of these (market, invasion rewards, etc.) are not listed.
guide.area: Pick a planet or node to see what it drops and the chances, stage by stage. Use the checkboxes to choose which kinds to show (resources, parts & blueprints, mods, relics, other).
guide.mastery: Tick off mastered Warframes and weapons and check your progress per category.
guide.mods: Look up where mods drop and tick the ones you own. Mod lists can also be read from a screenshot.
guide.arcane: Record the arcanes you own and their ranks.
guide.baro: See Baro's history list and this visit's items, checked against what you own.
guide.riven: See Riven prices per weapon from the official weekly stats.
guide.invasion: Shows the invasions in progress (location, rewards, progress) and every weapon part invasions give. Tick the parts you have collected.
guide.cycle: Day/night for the open worlds and the time until the daily and weekly resets. Also shows this week's Steel Essence exchange reward.
guide.duviri: This week's Duviri Circuit rewards and the coming rotation, for Normal and Steel Path.
guide.build: Save and manage your builds. Mods and more can be read from a screenshot (uses Windows text recognition).
guide.sim: Calculate frame stats, weapon DPS and Riven ranges.
guide.tips: Shows your own notes (.md / .csv / .txt). Edit the files in the tips folder to change it.
guide.update: Fetch the official data (drop tables, Japanese names, Riven prices, etc.). Run it after game updates.

mods.lead: Where every mod comes from (missions, enemies, bounties and more). Click a row for details, and tick the box on the left to record that you own it.
mods.placeholder: Mod name or target (e.g. Vitality / Khora)
scan.note: Open the mod screen in the game and scroll: mod names on screen are read and marked as owned (every few seconds, only when the screen changes). Low-confidence matches go to "Check"; click them if they are right. Reading uses Windows text recognition. Exclusive fullscreen may not be captured; use borderless (windowed) mode or read from screenshots instead.
mods.note: Chance: per reward roll for missions and bounties, per kill for enemies, and per opening for relics. "Not listed" means it is not in the official drop tables (syndicates, Baro, Nightwave, quest rewards and so on).
ms.lead: Mastery progress for Warframes, weapons, companions and more. Tick the box on the left to record it as mastered (saved on this PC).
ms.note: Kitguns count by chamber (primary and secondary versions separately), Zaws by strike, Amps by prism plus Sirocco, MOAs and Hounds by head (model), and K-Drives by board. Excalibur Prime, Skana Prime and Lato Prime are shown and counted under "Founder" only when "Founder" is checked. The Plexus and the Amp itself are under "Other". Mastery XP is the value up to max rank (200 per rank for Warframes, companions, sentinels, MOAs/Hounds, Archwings, Necramechs, K-Drives and the Plexus; 100 for weapons. Kuva, Tenet, Coda and similar weapons and Necramechs go to rank 40).
ac.title: Arcanes
ac.lead: Arcanes from the official data (ExportRelicArcane.json), grouped by what they equip on. Tick the box on the left to record one as owned and pick its rank (saved on this PC). You can filter by English or Japanese name.
ac.note: The type (what it equips on) is judged from the name (Arcane, Molt and Theorem are Warframe; Magus and Emergence are Operator; Virtuos and Eternal are Amp; Pax and Residual are Kitgun; Exodia is Zaw; and so on). New arcanes that cannot be judged go under "Other". Zid-An arcanes for the Tektolyst Artifact are not in the official data yet, so they are taken from the drop tables (English name only, no rarity, max rank 5; the official data is used once it has them). Seven arcanes that are in the official data but not in the game (Arcane Survival, Shield, Defense, Detoxifier, Liquid, Protection, Temperance) are left out. Unticking also clears the rank. New arcanes arrive with game updates, so fetch again with "Data Update".
baro.lead: Compares what Baro brought this time, and what Baro has brought before, with what you own. Mods are checked against the Mods list, weapons against the Mastery list (mastered), and cosmetics and similar items are ticked on this page (saved on this PC).
baro.note: The history list is a starting list built from the official data (fetched with "Data Update": weapons whose names start with Prisma, legendary mods whose names start with Primed, and Primed Chamber) plus the Baro visits recorded on this PC. This visit's items are fetched from the official World State only when you press "Update Baro info"; if Baro is here, the visit is recorded (new items are added, and "Last seen" and "Times" are updated for known ones). Past dates are unknown, so "Last seen" and "Times" only count visits recorded on this PC (TennoCon visits are not recorded). Items whose names end in Skin are treated as cosmetics. Items you can buy any number of times (consumables, boosters, relics and so on) are not checked. You can change which Primed mods are left out and which items are added in data/baro_rules.json in the tool's folder.

cyc.lead: Day/night and similar cycles, plus the time until the daily and weekly resets. Calculated from the cycle lengths, so it works offline.
cyc.note: "Sync with official data" asks the official World State only when pressed, and syncs the Plains and Zariman cycles and your PC clock offset (pressing again within 60 seconds reuses the last result). Orb Vallis and Duviri have no clue in the official data, so they are calculated from a reference time.

sim.f.head: Warframe and mods
sim.f.rb.note: Since Update 36 most Warframes get +100 health and shields and +50 energy. Fix it here for exceptions (Inaros, Nidus, etc.).

sim.note: These are estimates. Base Warframe and weapon stats come from the official Public Export (ExportWarframes / ExportWeapons); mod values, Riven base values and ability numbers come from public sources such as the WARFRAME Wiki. They can change with game updates, so adjust the inputs as needed. DPS does not include enemy armor, shields or weak points, status damage, combo multipliers, or special firing of charge/burst weapons.
sim.nodata: No simulator data yet. Fetch it with "Data Update" in the menu or the button on the right (needs an internet connection).
sim.fetching.log: Fetching. This can take a few tens of seconds...
sim.abil.head: Ability stats
sim.abil.ref: Abilities (enter a base value to estimate it with mods)
sim.f.note: Effective health = health ÷ (1 − damage reduction) + shields. Damage reduction = armor ÷ (armor + 300). Ability numbers (damage, range, etc.) are not in the official data, so enter base values you looked up on the WARFRAME Wiki or similar (inputs are saved in this PC's browser).
sim.w.note: Base damage: {list}. The weapon's innate elements are added after the elemental mods and combine with them.
sim.w.other: Not in this category. Found in:
sim.r.title: Ranges ({group} / disposition {dispo} / rank {rank})
sim.r.note: Value = base × disposition (fixed 1.2) × stat-count modifier × random (0.9–1.1). At rank r, × (r + 1) ÷ 9. Modifiers for this setup: positive ×{buff}{curse}. Base values are from the WARFRAME Wiki (some columns are estimated; Kitguns use pistol values and companion weapons use rifle values).

upd.lead: Fetches the drop tables, enemy and bounty sources, Riven prices and the name dictionary (including Riven dispositions and simulator data). Run it again after game updates.
upd.note: Sources: drop tables and sources come from WFCD/warframe-drop-data (drops.warframestat.us), names from calamity-inc/warframe-public-export (or the official Public Export if that fails), and Riven prices from the official weeklyRivensPC.json (or WFCD's api.warframestat.us). If the logo has not been fetched yet, it is also fetched from the official Warframe Fan Kit. An internet connection is required.
